findings.text: Strength: the first sentence tells a newcomer what Athena is. The next two leads explain what a 'study' is and why this page exists, so the reader isn't lost on landing.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: Strength: a link at the top jumps straight to concrete next steps, including an install command and a first request to try.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the "Next steps" section with "./setup.sh" and "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page is at Athena's address, but almost all of it describes a different project, firstmate. Athena gets one short paragraph. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work out that the rest is a worked example, not a description of Athena.
findings.source: title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the sections that follow (Start here through Claims and sources)

findings.text: The case for why Athena matters is thin. Features are listed, but nothing says what problem they solve or who should care. The traced-claims study is the only evidence of value, and the page never draws that conclusion for the reader.
findings.source: header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: This link is meant for the project's owner, but it sits in the newcomer's first screen with no explanation. It is likely to confuse a first-time visitor.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision"

findings.text: 'Ship', 'place', 'capacity' and 'exit 75' are used in the Start here section before they are defined. The 'Words used first' list leaves them out, so the reader has to scroll down to the Glossary.
findings.source: Start here > What firstmate is: "A ship changes a project; a local-only ship has no PR and lands by a guarded fast-forward." and One piece of work: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75"

findings.text: 'Captain call' and 'wake' are not defined anywhere on the page. The Glossary has 'captain' and 'stale wake', but it never says what a call or a wake is.
findings.source: "If the backlog item is still an open captain call, teardown reopens it"; "A stale wake shows the worker is stuck"

findings.text: The middle of the page (states, counters, eleven transition cards) is dense specialist material. A newcomer can skip it, but nothing tells them they may.
findings.source: Transitions cards, e.g. t8: "a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead"

findings.text: The install step lists no prerequisites, for example a Rust toolchain or AI model access. It also doesn't say what 'athena ask' will do to the user's repository, so a cautious newcomer may hold back from trying it.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh"
